questions.question: What is the primary purpose of tags in Robot Framework?

options.text: To classify and control test execution through flexible filtering
To define the execution order of tests within a suite
options.explanation: Tags are for classification and selection, not execution order

options.text: To enable parallel execution of multiple tests simultaneously
options.explanation: Tags don't control parallelization; they enable test selection

options.text: To specify timeout values for individual test cases
options.explanation: Timeouts are set with [Timeout] setting, not tags

questions.question: If a test is tagged with 'Smoke' and you run `robot --include smoke tests/`, what happens?

options.text: The test executes because tags are case-insensitive
The test is skipped because the case doesn't match
options.explanation: Tags are case-insensitive; 'Smoke' matches 'smoke'

options.text: Robot Framework throws a case mismatch error
options.explanation: No error occurs; tags are case-insensitive

options.text: The test executes only if lowercase was used in [Tags]
options.explanation: Tags are case-insensitive in both definition and filtering

questions.question: If a tag appears multiple times with different cases, which case is used in reports and logs?

options.text: The case of the first appearance of the tag
The case of the last appearance of the tag
options.explanation: The first appearance determines the case used in reports

options.text: All tags are converted to lowercase in reports
options.explanation: The case of the first appearance is preserved in reports

options.text: All tags are converted to uppercase in reports
options.explanation: The case of the first appearance is preserved in reports

questions.question: How can you assign tags to all tests|tasks in a suite?

options.text: Using the Test Tags setting in the *** Settings *** section
Using the [Tags] setting in each individual test|task
options.explanation: While this works, it's not efficient for all tests; Test Tags in *** Settings *** is the suite-level approach

options.text: Using the Suite Tags setting in the *** Settings *** section
options.explanation: The correct setting is Test Tags, not Suite Tags

options.text: Using the --tags command-line option
options.explanation: Command-line options filter execution; they don't assign tags

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Test Tags    smoke    regression
```

What is the effect of this setting?

options.text: All tests|tasks in the suite will have both 'smoke' and 'regression' tags
Only tests that don't have their own [Tags] will get these tags
options.explanation: Test Tags are added to all tests, even those with their own [Tags]

options.text: Tests must choose either 'smoke' or 'regression', not both
options.explanation: Both tags are applied to all tests

options.text: Only the first test in the suite gets these tags
options.explanation: All tests in the suite receive these tags

questions.question: How do you assign tags to an individual test|task?

options.text: Using the [Tags] setting within the test|task
Using the Test Tags setting in the test|task body
options.explanation: Test Tags is a suite-level setting; use [Tags] for individual tests

options.text: Using the @tags decorator before the test name
options.explanation: Robot Framework doesn't use decorators; use [Tags] setting

options.text: Using the TAG keyword in the test body
options.explanation: Use [Tags] setting; TAG is not a keyword for tag assignment (though Set Tags exists)

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Test Tags    smoke    regression

*** Test Cases ***
Valid Login Test
    [Tags]    login    critical
    Perform Login Steps
```

What tags will 'Valid Login Test' have?

options.text: smoke, regression, login, critical (suite tags plus test-specific tags)
Only login and critical (test [Tags] overrides suite tags)
options.explanation: [Tags] adds to suite tags, doesn't override them

options.text: Only smoke and regression (suite tags only)
options.explanation: Test-specific tags are added to suite tags

options.text: Only the first two tags: smoke and login
options.explanation: All tags from both sources are applied

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Test Tags    smoke    regression

*** Test Cases ***
Valid Login Test
    [Tags]    login    critical    -smoke
    Perform Login Steps
```

What tags will 'Valid Login Test' have?

options.text: regression, login, critical (smoke is removed by the minus sign)
smoke, regression, login, critical (minus sign has no effect)
options.explanation: The minus sign (-) before a tag removes it from the test's tags

options.text: login, critical, -smoke (minus sign is part of the tag name)
options.explanation: The minus sign removes the tag, it's not part of the tag name

options.text: Only smoke and regression (suite tags cannot be removed)
options.explanation: Suite tags can be removed using the minus sign prefix

questions.question: How do you remove a suite-level tag from a specific test|task?

options.text: Add a minus sign (-) before the tag name in the test's [Tags] setting
Use the NOT operator before the tag name
options.explanation: The minus sign (-) is the syntax for removing tags

options.text: Omit the [Tags] setting from the test
options.explanation: Omitting [Tags] keeps all suite tags; use minus sign to remove specific ones

options.text: Use [Tags] NONE to remove all inherited tags
options.explanation: While this might work, the question asks about removing specific tags, which uses the minus sign

questions.question:
```robot
*** Variables ***
${ENV}    production

*** Test Cases ***
Data Processing Test
    [Tags]    environment:${ENV}
    Process Data
```

What tag will this test have?

options.text: environment:production
environment:${ENV} (variables are not resolved in tags)
options.explanation: Variables are resolved in tags

options.text: environment and production (as two separate tags)
options.explanation: The colon is part of the tag name; it's a single tag

options.text: ${ENV} (the environment: prefix is ignored)
options.explanation: The entire string including the prefix becomes the tag

questions.question: Which built-in keywords can be used to dynamically assign or remove tags during test|task execution?

options.text: Set Tags
Remove Tags
Add Tags
options.explanation: The keyword is 'Set Tags', not 'Add Tags'

options.text: Clear Tags
options.explanation: The keyword is 'Remove Tags', not 'Clear Tags'

questions.question: What command-line option is used to include only tests|tasks that have a specific tag?

options.text: --include or -i
--tag or -t
options.explanation: The correct option is --include or -i

options.text: --select or -s
options.explanation: The correct option is --include or -i

options.text: --filter or -f
options.explanation: The correct option is --include or -i

questions.question:
```bash
robot --include smoke path/to/tests
```

What does this command do?

options.text: Executes only tests|tasks that have the 'smoke' tag
Executes all tests and adds the 'smoke' tag to them
options.explanation: --include filters execution; it doesn't add tags

options.text: Excludes tests with the 'smoke' tag
options.explanation: --include includes tests with the tag; --exclude excludes them

options.text: Generates a report of tests with the 'smoke' tag without executing them
options.explanation: --include executes the filtered tests

questions.question: What command-line option is used to exclude tests|tasks that have a specific tag?

options.text: --exclude or -e
--skip or -s
options.explanation: While --skip exists, --exclude is the option that excludes by tag

options.text: --ignore or -i
options.explanation: The correct option is --exclude or -e

options.text: --remove or -r
options.explanation: The correct option is --exclude or -e

questions.question:
```bash
robot --exclude slow path/to/tests
```

What happens to tests with the 'slow' tag?

options.text: They are not executed or logged at all
They are executed but marked as skipped in logs
options.explanation: --exclude completely excludes tests from execution and logs; --skip would mark them as skipped

options.text: They are executed with a warning
options.explanation: --exclude prevents execution entirely

options.text: They are logged but not executed
options.explanation: --exclude excludes them from both execution and logging

questions.question: What is the difference between --exclude and --skip for handling tests by tag?

options.text: --exclude removes tests from execution and logs entirely; --skip doesn't execute tests but includes them in logs as skipped
--exclude and --skip are identical in functionality
options.explanation: --exclude omits tests completely; --skip includes them as skipped in logs

options.text: --exclude only works with tags; --skip works with test names
options.explanation: Both can work with tags; the difference is in how they handle the tests

options.text: --skip is a deprecated alias for --exclude
options.explanation: Both are current options with different behaviors

questions.question:
```bash
robot --include regression --exclude unstable path/to/tests
```

Which tests will be executed?

options.text: Tests that have the 'regression' tag but not the 'unstable' tag
Tests that have either 'regression' or are not 'unstable'
options.explanation: Tests must have 'regression' AND not have 'unstable'

options.text: No tests (conflicting options)
options.explanation: The options work together to refine the selection

options.text: Only tests with both 'regression' and 'unstable' tags
options.explanation: Tests with 'unstable' are excluded, not included

questions.question: Why is it recommended to use lowercase tag names when filtering?

options.text: Because logical operators (AND, OR, NOT) are case-sensitive and uppercase
Because Robot Framework only recognizes lowercase tags
options.explanation: Tags are case-insensitive; the reason is to avoid conflicts with uppercase operators

options.text: Because uppercase tags are reserved for system use
options.explanation: Tags with robot: prefix are reserved; case doesn't determine reservation

options.text: Because lowercase tags execute faster
options.explanation: There is no performance difference; it's about operator conflicts

questions.question: What wildcard characters can be used in tag patterns?

options.text: * (matches any number of characters)
? (matches any single character)
+ (matches one or more characters)
options.explanation: The plus sign is not a wildcard in Robot Framework tag patterns

options.text: % (matches any character)
options.explanation: The percent sign is not a wildcard in Robot Framework tag patterns

questions.question:
```bash
robot --include feature-* path/to/tests
```

What does this command do?

options.text: Includes tests with tags starting with 'feature-'
Includes tests with exactly the tag 'feature-*'
options.explanation: The asterisk is a wildcard, not a literal character

options.text: Includes all tests and tags them with 'feature-*'
options.explanation: --include filters tests; it doesn't add tags

options.text: Includes tests in directories starting with 'feature-'
options.explanation: This filters by tag pattern, not directory names

questions.question:
```bash
robot --exclude *-deprecated path/to/tests
```

What does this command do?

options.text: Excludes tests with tags ending with '-deprecated'
Excludes tests with exactly the tag '*-deprecated'
options.explanation: The asterisk is a wildcard, not a literal character

options.text: Excludes all tests except those tagged 'deprecated'
options.explanation: It excludes tests with tags ending in '-deprecated'

options.text: Excludes deprecated Robot Framework features
options.explanation: This filters tests by tag pattern, not framework features

questions.question: What is the purpose of the wildcard ? in tag patterns?

options.text: To match any single character
To match any number of characters
options.explanation: The asterisk (*) matches any number; the question mark matches one

options.text: To indicate an optional tag
options.explanation: The question mark is a wildcard for single character matching

options.text: To mark a tag as uncertain in reports
options.explanation: The question mark is a wildcard character in patterns

questions.question: What prefix is reserved for internal use by Robot Framework and should not be used in user-defined tags?

options.text: robot:
rf:
options.explanation: The reserved prefix is 'robot:', not 'rf:'

options.text: system:
options.explanation: The reserved prefix is 'robot:'

options.text: internal:
options.explanation: The reserved prefix is 'robot:'

questions.question: What may happen if you use tags with the robot: prefix?

options.text: Unexpected behavior in test execution and reporting
The tags are automatically converted to user: prefix
options.explanation: Robot Framework doesn't convert the prefix; using it causes problems

options.text: Robot Framework raises an error and stops execution
options.explanation: It may cause unexpected behavior rather than an explicit error

options.text: The tags work normally but are hidden from reports
options.explanation: Using reserved prefixes causes unexpected behavior, not just hiding

questions.question: What is the purpose of the robot:exclude reserved tag?

options.text: Marks tests|tasks that should be excluded from execution, similar to --exclude
Marks tests that should be skipped but logged, similar to --skip
options.explanation: robot:exclude is for exclusion; robot:skip is for skipping

options.text: Removes tags from test metadata
options.explanation: robot:exclude controls test execution, not tag removal

options.text: Excludes tests from statistical reports but still executes them
options.explanation: robot:exclude prevents execution, not just reporting

questions.question: What is the purpose of the robot:skip reserved tag?

options.text: Marks tests|tasks that should be skipped during execution, similar to --skip
Marks tests that should be completely excluded from execution and logs
options.explanation: robot:skip skips tests but logs them; robot:exclude omits them entirely

options.text: Skips tag assignment for the test
options.explanation: robot:skip controls test execution, not tag assignment

options.text: Skips the test in reports but executes it normally
options.explanation: robot:skip prevents execution but includes in logs as skipped

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Test Tags    api    regression

*** Test Cases ***
Test A
    [Tags]    smoke
    Keyword A

Test B
    [Tags]    -api    critical
    Keyword B
```

What tags does Test A have?

options.text: api, regression, smoke
Only smoke (test tags override suite tags)
options.explanation: Test tags are added to suite tags, not replacing them

options.text: api, regression (suite tags only)
options.explanation: Test-specific tags are also applied

options.text: smoke, regression (api is removed)
options.explanation: Test A doesn't remove any tags; it only adds 'smoke'

questions.question:
```robot
*** Settings ***
Test Tags    api    regression

*** Test Cases ***
Test B
    [Tags]    -api    critical
    Keyword B
```

What tags does Test B have?

options.text: regression, critical (api is removed by -api)
api, regression, critical (minus sign is ignored)
options.explanation: The minus sign removes the api tag

options.text: api, regression, -api, critical (minus sign is part of tag name)
options.explanation: The minus sign is an operator that removes tags, not part of the name

options.text: Only critical (both suite tags are removed)
options.explanation: Only 'api' is removed; 'regression' remains

questions.question:
```bash
robot --include smoke --include regression path/to/tests
```

Which tests will be executed?

options.text: Tests that have either 'smoke' OR 'regression' tag (or both)
Tests that have both 'smoke' AND 'regression' tags
options.explanation: Multiple --include options use OR logic, not AND

options.text: Only tests with the 'smoke' tag (first option takes precedence)
options.explanation: Both options are applied with OR logic

options.text: No tests (conflicting options)
options.explanation: Multiple --include options are combined with OR logic

questions.question: Where can tags be used to create statistical summaries?

options.text: In the execution protocols (reports and logs)
Only in separate analytics tools outside Robot Framework
options.explanation: Robot Framework's own execution protocols include tag-based statistics

options.text: Only when using the --statistics command-line option
options.explanation: Tag statistics are automatically generated in execution protocols

options.text: Only in the rebot post-processing tool
options.explanation: Tag statistics are available in regular execution reports, not just rebot
